newsitem.title: USA: Amerin seeks meeting with NY Insurance Dept.
newsitem.headline: Amerin seeks meeting with NY Insurance Dept.

text.p: Amerin Corp said Tuesday it was seeking a meeting with the New York Insurance Department over its concerns regarding a recent department opinion about the legal status of captive mortgage reinsurance.

Amerin said it received a letter on March 20 from the department that stated, in the opinion of the department's general counsel, that captive reinsurance structures violate New York State insurance law.
Amerin said it does not believe that the issues raised by the department regarding captive mortgage reinsurance will have a material adverse effect on its business.
Amerin said it believes the letter was sent to all private mortgage insurance companies.

"We were surprised to receive the department's letter. In designing the captive reinsurance concept, we took extraordinary steps to ensure that it complies with all applicable federal and state regulations," Amerin Chairman Gerald Friedman said in a statement.

He said Amerin met with the New York Insurance Department within the past two years to discuss a specific captive reinsurance program. "At that time, and until we received the letter, the department had voiced no issues with the concept," Friedman said.

Although it is a relatively new concept, captive reinsurance has been approved by the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency and by various mortgage agencies, Amerin said. It is being studied or implemented by several major commercial banks and mortgage companies.
Amerin provides private mortgage insurance to leading mortgage originators.
